question_text: (5 marks): CALCULUS -- LINEAR DIFFERENTIAL EQUATION ============================================================ Solve the linear differential equation: dy/dx + 3y = e^x. [5] Answer: This is a linear first-order DE of the form dy/dx + Py = Q, where P = 3, Q = e^x. Step 1: Find the integrating factor (IF). IF = e^(integralP dx) = e^(integral3 dx) = e^(3x) Step 2: Multiply both sides by IF. e^(3x) x dy/dx + 3e^(3x) x y = e^(3x) x e^x e^(3x) x dy/dx + 3e^(3x) x y = e^(4x) The left side is the derivative of y x e^(3x) (by the product rule in reverse): d/dx[y x e^(3x)] = e^(4x) Step 3: Integrate both sides. y x e^(3x) = integrale^(4x) dx = e^(4x)/4 + C Step 4: Solve for y. y = e^(-3x) x [e^(4x)/4 + C] y = e^(4x - 3x)/4 + C e^(-3x) y = e^x/4 + C e^(-3x) Marking: 1 for identifying P and Q, 1 for IF = e^(3x), 1 for multiplying through, 1 for integrating, 1 for solving for y. Target node: c12_maths_003 ============================================================
answer_text: Answer: y = e^x/4 + C e^(-3x)

question_text: (6 marks): VECTORS AND 3D GEOMETRY ============================================================ (a) Find a x b if a = (1, 0, 0) and b = (0, 1, 0). Verify that a x b is perpendicular to both a and b. [3] Answer: |1  0  0| |0  1  0| = i(0x0 - 0x1) - j(1x0 - 0x0) + k(1x1 - 0x0) = i(0) - j(0) + k(1) = (0, 0, 1) Verification: (a x b) x a = (0)(1) + (0)(0) + (1)(0) = 0 OK (perpendicular to a) (a x b) x b = (0)(0) + (0)(1) + (1)(0) = 0 OK (perpendicular to b) Marking: 1 for cross product calculation, 1 for correct result, 1 for verification. Target node: c12_maths_005 (b) Find the angle between vectors a = (1, 1, 0) and b = (0, 1, 1). [3] Answer: Step 1: Find a x b. Step 2: Find |a| and |b|. |a| = sqrt(1 + 1 + 0) = sqrt2 |b| = sqrt(0 + 1 + 1) = sqrt2 Step 3: Use the dot product formula. 1 = sqrt2 x sqrt2 x cos theta 1 = 2 cos theta cos theta = 1/2 theta = 60 deg  = pi/3 radians Marking: 1 for dot product, 1 for magnitudes, 1 for finding theta. Target node: c12_maths_005 ============================================================
answer_text: Answer: The angle between a and b is 60 deg  (pi/3 radians).

question_text: (5 marks): LINEAR PROGRAMMING ============================================================ Minimise Z = 2x + 3y subject to the constraints: x + y >= 4, x <= 3, y <= 2, x >= 0, y >= 0. [5] Answer: Step 1: Plot the constraints on graph paper. - x + y >= 4: line through (4, 0) and (0, 4). Shade ABOVE the line. - x <= 3: vertical line at x = 3. Shade LEFT. - y <= 2: horizontal line at y = 2. Shade BELOW. - x >= 0: right of y-axis. - y >= 0: above x-axis. Step 2: Find the feasible region and corner points. The feasible region is the area satisfying ALL constraints. Corner points: - Intersection of x + y = 4 and x = 3: (3, 1) - Intersection of x = 3 and y = 2: (3, 2) - Check if (2, 2) is feasible: 2 + 2 = 4 >= 4 OK, 2 <= 3 OK, 2 <= 2 OK. Yes, (2, 2) is a corner point. Corner points: (3, 1), (3, 2), (2, 2) Step 3: Evaluate Z at each corner point. Z(3, 1) = 2(3) + 3(1) = 6 + 3 = 9 Z(3, 2) = 2(3) + 3(2) = 6 + 6 = 12 Z(2, 2) = 2(2) + 3(2) = 4 + 6 = 10 Step 4: Find the minimum. Minimum Z = 9 at (x, y) = (3, 1). [DIAGRAM: Graph on graph paper showing the feasible region with corner points labelled. The optimal point (3, 1) is marked.] Marking: 1 for graph/constraints, 1 for feasible region, 1 for corner points, 1 for evaluating Z, 1 for identifying minimum. Target node: c12_maths_006 ============================================================
answer_text: Answer: Minimum Z = 9 at (3, 1).

question_text: (9 marks): PROBABILITY ============================================================ (a) If P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5, and P(A intersection B) = 0.3, determine whether A and B are independent events. [3] Answer: Check: P(A) x P(B) = 0.6 x 0.5 = 0.30 Given: P(A intersection B) = 0.3 = 0.30 Since P(A intersection B) = P(A) x P(B), events A and B ARE independent. Marking: 1 for stating the condition, 1 for calculating P(A)xP(B), 1 for conclusion. Target node: c12_maths_007 (b) A die is thrown 6 times. Find the probability of getting exactly 4 sixes. [3] Answer: This is a binomial distribution problem. n = 6 (number of trials), p = 1/6 (probability of a six), q = 5/6 (probability of not a six) P(X = 4) = C(6,4) x p^4 x q^2 = 6!/(4! x 2!) x (1/6)^4 x (5/6)^2 = 15 x (1/1296) x (25/36) = 15 x 25 / (1296 x 36) = 375 / 46656 ~= 0.00804 Marking: 1 for identifying binomial, 1 for correct formula, 1 for calculation. Target node: c12_maths_007 (c) A factory has two machines M1 and M2. M1 produces 60% of the items and M2 produces 40%. The defective rates are 2% for M1 and 3% for M2. If a randomly selected item is found to be defective, what is the probability that it was produced by M1? [3] Answer: Using Bayes' Theorem: Given: P(M1) = 0.60, P(M2) = 0.40 P(D|M1) = 0.02, P(D|M2) = 0.03 Step 1: Find P(D) using the Law of Total Probability. P(D) = P(M1) x P(D|M1) + P(M2) x P(D|M2) P(D) = 0.60 x 0.02 + 0.40 x 0.03 P(D) = 0.012 + 0.012 = 0.024 Step 2: Apply Bayes' Theorem. P(M1|D) = P(D|M1) x P(M1) / P(D) P(M1|D) = (0.02 x 0.60) / 0.024 P(M1|D) = 0.012 / 0.024 P(M1|D) = 0.5 = 1/2 Marking: 1 for P(D) using total probability, 1 for Bayes' formula, 1 for final answer. Target node: c12_maths_007 ============================================================ ADDITIONAL PRACTICE QUESTIONS WITH FULL SOLUTIONS ============================================================ ============================================================
answer_text: Answer: P(item from M1 | defective) = 0.5 (50%)

question_text: (10 marks): RELATIONS AND FUNCTIONS -- ADVANCED ============================================================ (a) Let R be a relation on Z (integers) defined by: aRb if and only if a - b is divisible by 3. Prove that R is an equivalence relation. [5] Answer: Reflexive: a - a = 0, which is divisible by 3. So aRa OK Symmetric: If aRb, then 3 | (a - b) -> 3 | -(a - b) = (b - a). So bRa OK Transitive: If aRb and bRc, then 3 | (a-b) and 3 | (b-c). So 3 | [(a-b) + (b-c)] = (a-c). So aRc OK Since R is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive, R is an equivalence relation. Marking: 1 for reflexive, 1 for symmetric, 1 for transitive, 1 for each proof, 1 for conclusion. Target node: c12_maths_001 (b) If f: R -> R is defined by f(x) = 3x - 5, prove that f is bijective and find f^-^1. [5] Answer: Injective: f(x_1) = f(x_2) -> 3x_1 - 5 = 3x_2 - 5 -> 3x_1 = 3x_2 -> x_1 = x_2 OK Surjective: For any y in R, let x = (y + 5)/3. Then f(x) = 3(y+5)/3 - 5 = y + 5 - 5 = y OK Since f is both injective and surjective, f is bijective. f^-^1(y) = (y + 5)/3, so f^-^1(x) = (x + 5)/3 Marking: 1 for injective proof, 1 for surjective proof, 1 for bijective conclusion, 1 for finding x, 1 for f^-^1. Target node: c12_maths_001 ============================================================

(10 marks): CALCULUS -- INTEGRATION ADVANCED ============================================================ (a) Evaluate integral(0 to pi/2) cos^2(x) dx. [5] Answer: Using cos^2x = (1 + cos(2x))/2: integral(0 to pi/2) cos^2x dx = integral(0 to pi/2) (1 + cos(2x))/2 dx = (1/2)[x + sin(2x)/2](0 to pi/2) = (1/2)[(pi/2 + sin(pi)/2) - (0 + 0)] = (1/2)(pi/2 + 0) = pi/4 Marking: 1 for double angle identity, 1 for splitting integral, 1 for integrating, 1 for limits, 1 for answer. Target node: c12_maths_003 (b) Evaluate integraldx / (x^2 + 4x + 5). [5] Answer: x^2 + 4x + 5 = (x^2 + 4x + 4) + 1 = (x + 2)^2 + 1 integraldx / [(x+2)^2 + 1] = tan^-^1(x + 2) + C (Using: integraldu/(u^2 + a^2) = (1/a)tan^-^1(u/a) + C, here a = 1) Marking: 1 for completing square, 1 for substitution, 1 for standard form, 1 for formula, 1 for answer. Target node: c12_maths_003 ============================================================

(8 marks): VECTORS AND 3D -- ADVANCED ============================================================ (a) Find the shortest distance between the skew lines: L1: r = (i + 2j + 3k) + t(2i + j + k) L2: r = (2i + 3j + k) + s(i + 2j + 3k) [4] Answer: a1 = (1, 2, 3), b1 = (2, 1, 1), a2 = (2, 3, 1), b2 = (1, 2, 3) a2 - a1 = (1, 1, -2) Shortest distance = |(a2-a1)x(b1xb2)| / |b1xb2| b1 x b2 = |i j k; 2 1 1; 1 2 3| = i(3-2) - j(6-1) + k(4-1) = (1, -5, 3) |b1 x b2| = sqrt(1 + 25 + 9) = sqrt35 (a2-a1)x(b1xb2) = (1)(1) + (1)(-5) + (-2)(3) = 1 - 5 - 6 = -10 d = |-10|/sqrt35 = 10/sqrt35 = 10sqrt35/35 = 2sqrt35/7 Marking: 1 for formula, 1 for b1xb2, 1 for dot product, 1 for answer. Target node: c12_maths_005 (b) Find the equation of the plane passing through (1, 1, 1), (2, 0, 3), and (0, 1, 2). [4] Answer: Let A = (1,1,1), B = (2,0,3), C = (0,1,2) AB = (1, -1, 2), AC = (-1, 0, 1) Normal n = AB x AC = |i j k; 1 -1 2; -1 0 1| = i(-1-0) - j(1+2) + k(0-1) = (-1, -3, -1) Equation: -1(x-1) - 3(y-1) - 1(z-1) = 0 -x + 1 - 3y + 3 - z + 1 = 0 -x - 3y - z + 5 = 0 x + 3y + z = 5 Marking: 1 for vectors, 1 for cross product, 1 for plane equation, 1 for simplification. (6 marks): PROBABILITY -- ADVANCED ============================================================ (a) A box contains 3 red and 5 white balls. Two balls are drawn at random one by one without replacement. Find the probability that both are red. [3] Answer: P(first red) = 3/8 P(second red | first red) = 2/7 P(both red) = 3/8 x 2/7 = 6/56 = 3/28 Marking: 1 for first probability, 1 for conditional, 1 for answer. Target node: c12_maths_007 (b) X is a random variable with probability distribution: X: 0, 1, 2, 3 P(X): 0.1, k, 2k, 0.4 Find k, E(X), and Var(X). [3] Answer: Sum of probabilities = 1: 0.1 + k + 2k + 0.4 = 1 -> 3k = 0.5 -> k = 1/6 E(X) = 0(0.1) + 1(1/6) + 2(2/6) + 3(0.4) = 0 + 1/6 + 4/6 + 1.2 = 5/6 + 1.2 = 5/6 + 6/5 = (25+36)/30 = 61/30 E(X^2) = 0(0.1) + 1(1/6) + 4(2/6) + 9(0.4) = 1/6 + 8/6 + 3.6 = 9/6 + 3.6 = 1.5 + 3.6 = 5.1 Var(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2 = 5.1 - (61/30)^2 = 5.1 - 3721/900 = 4590/900 - 3721/900 = 869/900 ~= 0.966 Marking: 1 for finding k, 1 for E(X), 1 for Var(X). Remember the correct formula: P(M1|D) = P(D|M1) x P(M1) / P(D). The posterior probability P(M1|D) updates the prior P(M1) using new evidence (the item is defective). Write the time. [2] (a) If the short hand is on 3 and the long hand is on 12, the time is ___. [1] (b) If the short hand is on 7 and the long hand is on 6, the time is ___. [1]
Complete the pattern. [2] (a) 5, 10, 15, ___, ___, ___ [1] (b) 100, 90, 80, ___, ___, ___ [1] === MARKING SCHEME (with step-by-step solutions) ===

Fill in the blanks. (a) 101, 103 -- Solution: Count forward from 100: 100, 101, 102, 103, 104. Missing are 101 and 103. (b) 160 -- Solution: The number after 159 is 159 + 1 = 160. (c) 1 -- Solution: 10 tens = 10 x 10 = 100 = 1 hundred. (d) 146 -- Solution: The number between 145 and 147 is 146 (145 + 1 = 146). (e) 198, 196 -- Solution: Count backward from 200: 200, 199, 198, 197, 196. Missing are 198 and 196. [1 each]

Addition (with carry). (a) 43 -- Solution: 25 + 18. Ones: 5 + 8 = 13. Write 3, carry 1. Tens: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Answer: 43. (b) 83 -- Solution: 47 + 36. Ones: 7 + 6 = 13. Write 3, carry 1. Tens: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. Answer: 83. (c) 87 -- Solution: 58 + 29. Ones: 8 + 9 = 17. Write 7, carry 1. Tens: 5 + 2 + 1 = 8. Answer: 87. (d) 90 -- Solution: 63 + 27. Ones: 3 + 7 = 10. Write 0, carry 1. Tens: 6 + 2 + 1 = 9. Answer: 90. (e) 100 -- Solution: 85 + 15. Ones: 5 + 5 = 10. Write 0, carry 1. Tens: 8 + 1 + 1 = 10. Write 10. Answer: 100. [1 each -- must show carry]

Subtraction (with borrow). (a) 15 -- Solution: 32 - 17. Ones: 2 - 7, can't do. Borrow 1 ten: 12 - 7 = 5. Tens: 2 - 1 - 1 = 1. Answer: 15. (b) 26 -- Solution: 50 - 24. Ones: 0 - 4, can't do. Borrow: 10 - 4 = 6. Tens: 4 - 2 = 2. Answer: 26. (c) 36 -- Solution: 74 - 38. Ones: 4 - 8, can't do. Borrow: 14 - 8 = 6. Tens: 6 - 3 = 3. Answer: 36. (d) 45 -- Solution: 90 - 45. Ones: 0 - 5, can't do. Borrow: 10 - 5 = 5. Tens: 8 - 4 = 4. Answer: 45. (e) 64 -- Solution: 100 - 36. Borrow from hundreds: 100 -> 90 + 10. Ones: 10 - 6 = 4. Tens: 9 - 3 = 6. Answer: 64. [1 each -- must show borrow]

Multiplication. (a) 10 -- Solution: 2 x 5 means 2 groups of 5: 5 + 5 = 10. (b) 12 -- Solution: 3 x 4 means 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. (c) 12 -- Solution: 4 x 3 means 4 groups of 3: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12. (d) 10 -- Solution: 5 x 2 means 5 groups of 2: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10. (e) 16 -- Solution: 2 x 8 means 2 groups of 8: 8 + 8 = 16. [1 each]

Word problems. (a) 27 mangoes -- Solution: 45 mangoes - 18 sold = 45 - 18. Ones: 5 - 8, borrow: 15 - 8 = 7. Tens: 3 - 1 = 2. Answer: 27 mangoes. (b) 43 children -- Solution: 24 girls + 19 boys = 24 + 19. Ones: 4 + 9 = 13, carry 1. Tens: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Answer: 43 children. (c) 20 pencils -- Solution: 5 pencils per box x 4 boxes = 5 x 4 = 20 pencils. [2 each -- 1 for method, 1 for answer]
Time. (a) 3 o'clock -- Solution: Short hand = hour = 3. Long hand on 12 = 00 minutes. Time: 3:00 or 3 o'clock. (b) 7:30 -- Solution: Short hand = 7. Long hand on 6 = 30 minutes. Time: 7:30. [1 each]
Patterns. (a) 20, 25, 30 -- Solution: Count by 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. (b) 70, 60, 50 -- Solution: Count backward by 10: 100, 90, 80, 70, 60, 50. [1 each] === ADDITIONAL PRACTICE QUESTIONS ===

Write the place value. [5] (a) In 365, the digit in the hundreds place is ___. [1] (b) In 248, the value of 4 is ___. [1] (c) In 519, the digit in the ones place is ___. [1] (d) In 703, the value of 7 is ___. [1] (e) Write 186 in expanded form: ___ + ___ + ___ [1]

Measurement. [5] (a) 1 metre = ___ centimetres [1] (b) 50 cm + 30 cm = ___ cm [1] (c) A pencil is 12 cm long. A pen is 8 cm long. Total length = ___ cm [1] (d) 1 litre = ___ millilitres [1] (e) A bottle has 500 ml of water. 200 ml is poured out. How much is left? ___ ml [1]

Time. [5] (a) There are ___ minutes in 1 hour. [1] (b) The short hand is on 5 and the long hand is on 12. The time is ___. [1] (c) The short hand is on 10 and the long hand is on 6. The time is ___. [1] (d) If it is 9 o'clock now, what time will it be after 2 hours? ___ [1] (e) There are ___ months in a year. [1]

Word problems. [5] (a) A fruit seller has 85 oranges. He sells 47. How many are left? [1] (b) There are 32 red flowers and 28 yellow flowers. How many flowers in all? [1] (c) Each child has 4 pencils. There are 6 children. How many pencils in all? [1] (d) A string is 45 cm long. 18 cm is cut. How much is left? [1] (e) A box has 24 sweets. 12 are eaten. How many are left? [1]

Money. [5] (a) Rs 1 = ___ paise [1] (b) A notebook costs Rs 15. A pen costs Rs 12. Total cost = Rs ___ [1] (c) You have Rs 50. You spend Rs 28. How much is left? Rs ___ [1] (d) 2 fifty-paise coins make Rs ___ [1] (e) A chocolate costs Rs 8. How much do 3 chocolates cost? Rs ___ [1]
Compare using >, < or =. [5] (a) 156 ___ 165 [1] (b) 98 ___ 101 [1] (c) 250 ___ 250 [1] (d) 199 ___ 200 [1] (e) 300 ___ 299 [1] === ADDITIONAL MARKING SCHEME (with step-by-step solutions) ===

Place value. (a) 3 -- Solution: In 365, the hundreds place is the leftmost digit = 3. (b) 40 -- Solution: In 248, the digit 4 is in the tens place. Value = 4 x 10 = 40. (c) 9 -- Solution: In 519, the ones place is the rightmost digit = 9. (d) 700 -- Solution: In 703, the digit 7 is in the hundreds place. Value = 7 x 100 = 700. (e) 100 + 80 + 6 -- Solution: 186 = 1 hundred + 8 tens + 6 ones = 100 + 80 + 6. [1 each]

Addition with carry. (a) 83 -- Solution: 36 + 47. Ones: 6 + 7 = 13, carry 1. Tens: 3 + 4 + 1 = 8. Answer: 83. (b) 87 -- Solution: 59 + 28. Ones: 9 + 8 = 17, carry 1. Tens: 5 + 2 + 1 = 8. Answer: 87. (c) 92 -- Solution: 73 + 19. Ones: 3 + 9 = 12, carry 1. Tens: 7 + 1 + 1 = 9. Answer: 92. (d) 113 -- Solution: 68 + 45. Ones: 8 + 5 = 13, carry 1. Tens: 6 + 4 + 1 = 11. Answer: 113. (e) 131 -- Solution: 94 + 37. Ones: 4 + 7 = 11, carry 1. Tens: 9 + 3 + 1 = 13. Answer: 131. [1 each -- must show carry]

Subtraction with borrow. (a) 23 -- Solution: 52 - 29. Ones: 2 - 9, borrow: 12 - 9 = 3. Tens: 4 - 2 = 2. Answer: 23. (b) 45 -- Solution: 81 - 36. Ones: 1 - 6, borrow: 11 - 6 = 5. Tens: 7 - 3 = 4. Answer: 45. (c) 17 -- Solution: 65 - 48. Ones: 5 - 8, borrow: 15 - 8 = 7. Tens: 5 - 4 = 1. Answer: 17. (d) 36 -- Solution: 93 - 57. Ones: 3 - 7, borrow: 13 - 7 = 6. Tens: 8 - 5 = 3. Answer: 36. (e) 59 -- Solution: 108 - 49. Ones: 8 - 9, borrow: 18 - 9 = 9. Tens: 9 - 4 = 5. Answer: 59. [1 each -- must show borrow]

Multiplication. (a) 18 -- Solution: 3 x 6 = 3 groups of 6: 6 + 6 + 6 = 18. (b) 20 -- Solution: 4 x 5 = 4 groups of 5: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20. (c) 15 -- Solution: 5 x 3 = 5 groups of 3: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 15. (d) 18 -- Solution: 2 x 9 = 2 groups of 9: 9 + 9 = 18. (e) 16 -- Solution: 4 x 4 = 4 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16. [1 each]

Number names. (a) one hundred twenty-five -- Solution: 125 = 1 hundred + 2 tens + 5 ones. (b) two hundred fifty -- Solution: 250 = 2 hundreds + 5 tens + 0 ones. (c) three hundred seventy-eight -- Solution: 378 = 3 hundreds + 7 tens + 8 ones. (d) five hundred -- Solution: 500 = 5 hundreds. (e) nine hundred ninety-nine -- Solution: 999 = 9 hundreds + 9 tens + 9 ones. [1 each]

Measurement. (a) 100 cm -- Solution: 1 metre = 100 centimetres. (b) 80 cm -- Solution: 50 cm + 30 cm = 80 cm. (c) 20 cm -- Solution: Pencil 12 cm + Pen 8 cm = 12 + 8 = 20 cm total. (d) 1000 ml -- Solution: 1 litre = 1000 millilitres. (e) 300 ml -- Solution: 500 ml - 200 ml = 300 ml left. [1 each]

Time. (a) 60 minutes -- Solution: 1 hour = 60 minutes. (b) 5 o'clock -- Solution: Short hand on 5 = hour 5. Long hand on 12 = 00 min. Time: 5:00. (c) 10:30 -- Solution: Short hand on 10 = hour 10. Long hand on 6 = 30 min. Time: 10:30. (d) 11 o'clock -- Solution: 9 o'clock + 2 hours = 9 + 2 = 11 o'clock. (e) 12 months -- Solution: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec = 12 months. [1 each]

Word problems. (a) 38 oranges -- Solution: 85 - 47. Ones: 5 - 7, borrow: 15 - 7 = 8. Tens: 7 - 4 = 3. Answer: 38 oranges. (b) 60 flowers -- Solution: 32 + 28. Ones: 2 + 8 = 10, carry 1. Tens: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 60 flowers. (c) 24 pencils -- Solution: 4 pencils x 6 children = 4 x 6 = 24 pencils. (d) 27 cm -- Solution: 45 cm - 18 cm. Ones: 5 - 8, borrow: 15 - 8 = 7. Tens: 3 - 1 = 2. Answer: 27 cm. (e) 12 sweets -- Solution: 24 - 12. Ones: 4 - 2 = 2. Tens: 2 - 1 = 1. Answer: 12 sweets. [1 each]

Patterns. (a) 140, 150, 160 -- Solution: Count by 10: 110, 120, 130, 140, 150, 160. (b) 65, 55, 45 -- Solution: Count backward by 10: 95, 85, 75, 65, 55, 45. (c) 10, 12 -- Solution: Count by 2: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. (d) circle, triangle -- Solution: Pattern repeats "triangle, triangle, circle". After "triangle, triangle, circle, triangle, triangle" comes "circle, triangle". (e) 165, 170, 175 -- Solution: Count by 5: 150, 155, 160, 165, 170, 175. [1 each]

Money. (a) 100 paise -- Solution: Rs 1 = 100 paise. (b) Rs 27 -- Solution: Rs 15 + Rs 12 = 15 + 12 = Rs 27. (c) Rs 22 -- Solution: Rs 50 - Rs 28. Ones: 0 - 8, borrow: 10 - 8 = 2. Tens: 4 - 2 = 2. Answer: Rs 22. (d) Re 1 -- Solution: 2 fifty-paise coins = 50 + 50 = 100 paise = Re 1. (e) Rs 24 -- Solution: Rs 8 x 3 = 8 + 8 + 8 = Rs 24. [1 each]

Compare (> , < or =). (a) < -- Solution: 156 vs 165. Hundreds same (1). Tens: 5 < 6. So 156 < 165. (b) < -- Solution: 98 has 9 tens, 101 has 10 tens. 98 < 101. (c) = -- Solution: 250 and 250 are equal. 250 = 250. (d) < -- Solution: 199 vs 200. 199 < 200 (199 is one less than 200). (e) > -- Solution: 300 vs 299. 300 is one more than 299. 300 > 299. [1 each] VOCABULARY: addition, subtraction, multiplication, carry, borrow, word problems, time, patterns. SCOPE_BOUNDARY: Class 2 Mathematics mock paper. For C3 mock paper, see c3_mock_icse_maths. Ask an adult to check using the marking scheme. TEXT_WALKTHROUGH: Section A covers numbers, addition with carry, subtraction with borrow, and multiplication. Section B has word problems, time, and patterns. Total: 30 marks, 1 hour. TEXT_REFERENCE: ICSE Class 2 Mathematics Syllabus (CISCE).

Fill in the blanks. [5] (a) 500, ___, 502, ___, 504 [1] (b) 999 + 1 = ___ [1] (c) 10 hundreds = ___ thousand. [1] (d) The place value of 7 in 745 is ___. [1] (e) Write 836 in expanded form: ___ + ___ + ___ [1]

Write as fractions. [5] (a) 2 out of 3 equal parts = ___ [1] (b) 1 out of 4 equal parts = ___ [1] (c) 3 out of 5 equal parts = ___ [1] (d) 2 out of 2 equal parts = ___ [1] (e) 1 out of 2 equal parts = ___ [1] === SECTION B (15 MARKS -- COMPULSORY) ===

Solve the word problems. [10] (a) A school has 345 boys and 267 girls. How many children in total? [2] (b) A fruit seller had 450 apples. He sold 278. How many are left? [2] (c) Each box has 6 pens. There are 8 boxes. How many pens in all? [2] (d) Rs50 was spent on a book and Rs25 on a pen. How much was spent in total? How much is left from Rs100? [3] (e) A ribbon is 75 cm long. 28 cm is cut off. How much is left? [1]

Complete the pattern. [2] (a) 100, 150, 200, ___, ___, ___ [1] (b) 3, 6, 9, ___, ___, ___ [1] === MARKING SCHEME (with step-by-step solutions) ===

Fill in the blanks. (a) 501, 503 -- Solution: Count forward from 500: 500, 501, 502, 503, 504. Missing are 501 and 503. (b) 1000 -- Solution: 999 + 1 = 1000 (the smallest 4-digit number). (c) 1 -- Solution: 10 hundreds = 10 x 100 = 1000 = 1 thousand. (d) 700 -- Solution: In 745, the digit 7 is in the hundreds place. Place value = 7 x 100 = 700. (e) 800 + 30 + 6 -- Solution: 836 = 8 hundreds + 3 tens + 6 ones = 800 + 30 + 6. [1 each]

Addition (3-digit, show working). (a) 563 -- Solution: 345 + 218. Ones: 5 + 8 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Tens: 4 + 1 + 1 = 6. Hundreds: 3 + 2 = 5. Answer: 563. (b) 856 -- Solution: 567 + 289. Ones: 7 + 9 = 16, write 6 carry 1. Tens: 6 + 8 + 1 = 15, write 5 carry 1. Hundreds: 5 + 2 + 1 = 8. Answer: 856. (c) 923 -- Solution: 728 + 195. Ones: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Tens: 2 + 9 + 1 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Hundreds: 7 + 1 + 1 = 9. Answer: 923. (d) 803 -- Solution: 406 + 397. Ones: 6 + 7 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Tens: 0 + 9 + 1 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Hundreds: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. Answer: 803. (e) 1001 -- Solution: 835 + 166. Ones: 5 + 6 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Tens: 3 + 6 + 1 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Hundreds: 8 + 1 + 1 = 10, write 10. Answer: 1001. [1 each -- must show working]

Subtraction (3-digit, show working). (a) 337 -- Solution: 524 - 187. Ones: 4 - 7, borrow: 14 - 7 = 7. Tens: 1 - 8, borrow: 11 - 8 = 3. Hundreds: 4 - 1 = 3. Answer: 337. (b) 355 -- Solution: 700 - 345. Ones: 0 - 5, borrow: 10 - 5 = 5. Tens: 9 - 4 = 5. Hundreds: 6 - 3 = 3. Answer: 355. (c) 344 -- Solution: 812 - 468. Ones: 2 - 8, borrow: 12 - 8 = 4. Tens: 0 - 6, borrow: 10 - 6 = 4. Hundreds: 7 - 4 = 3. Answer: 344. (d) 325 -- Solution: 600 - 275. Ones: 0 - 5, borrow: 10 - 5 = 5. Tens: 9 - 7 = 2. Hundreds: 5 - 2 = 3. Answer: 325. (e) 487 -- Solution: 905 - 418. Ones: 5 - 8, borrow: 15 - 8 = 7. Tens: 9 - 1 = 8. Hundreds: 8 - 4 = 4. Answer: 487. [1 each -- must show working]

Multiplication (2-digit x 1-digit). (a) 102 -- Solution: 34 x 3. 4 x 3 = 12, write 2 carry 1. 3 x 3 = 9, + 1 = 10. Answer: 102. (b) 224 -- Solution: 56 x 4. 6 x 4 = 24, write 4 carry 2. 5 x 4 = 20, + 2 = 22. Answer: 224. (c) 360 -- Solution: 72 x 5. 2 x 5 = 10, write 0 carry 1. 7 x 5 = 35, + 1 = 36. Answer: 360. (d) 288 -- Solution: 48 x 6. 8 x 6 = 48, write 8 carry 4. 4 x 6 = 24, + 4 = 28. Answer: 288. (e) 651 -- Solution: 93 x 7. 3 x 7 = 21, write 1 carry 2. 9 x 7 = 63, + 2 = 65. Answer: 651. [1 each]

Fractions. (a) 2/3 -- Solution: 2 out of 3 equal parts = 2/3. Numerator = 2 (parts taken), denominator = 3 (total parts). (b) 1/4 -- Solution: 1 out of 4 equal parts = 1/4. (c) 3/5 -- Solution: 3 out of 5 equal parts = 3/5. (d) 2/2 = 1 -- Solution: 2 out of 2 equal parts = 2/2 = 1 (the whole). (e) 1/2 -- Solution: 1 out of 2 equal parts = 1/2 (one half). [1 each]

Word problems. (a) 612 children -- Solution: 345 boys + 267 girls. Ones: 5+7=12, carry 1. Tens: 4+6+1=11, carry 1. Hundreds: 3+2+1=6. Answer: 612. (b) 172 apples -- Solution: 450 - 278. Ones: 0-8, borrow: 10-8=2. Tens: 4-7, borrow: 14-7=7. Hundreds: 3-2=1. Answer: 172. (c) 48 pens -- Solution: 6 pens x 8 boxes = 6 x 8 = 48 pens. (d) Rs75 spent, Rs25 left -- Solution: Spent = 50 + 25 = Rs75. Left = 100 - 75. Ones: 0-5, borrow: 10-5=5. Tens: 9-7=2. Answer: Rs25 left. (e) 47 cm -- Solution: 75 cm - 28 cm. Ones: 5-8, borrow: 15-8=7. Tens: 6-2=4. Answer: 47 cm. [marks as shown]

Time. (a) 4:15 -- Solution: Short hand on 4 = hour 4. Long hand on 3 = 15 minutes. Time: 4:15. (b) 9:00 -- Solution: Short hand on 9 = hour 9. Long hand on 12 = 00 minutes. Time: 9:00. (c) 2:30 -- Solution: Short hand between 2 and 3 = hour 2. Long hand on 6 = 30 minutes. Time: 2:30. [1 each]
Patterns. (a) 250, 300, 350 -- Solution: Count by 50: 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350. (b) 12, 15, 18 -- Solution: Count by 3: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. [1 each] === ADDITIONAL PRACTICE QUESTIONS ===

[1] (e) A tank has 500 litres of water. 125 litres are used. How much is left? [1] === ADDITIONAL MARKING SCHEME (with step-by-step solutions) ===

Fill in the blanks. (a) 1000 -- Solution: The smallest 4-digit number is 1000 (1 thousand, 0 hundreds, 0 tens, 0 ones). (b) 999 -- Solution: The largest 3-digit number is 999 (9 hundreds, 9 tens, 9 ones). (c) 5,000 -- Solution: In 5,237, the digit 5 is in the thousands place. Place value = 5 x 1000 = 5,000. (d) 4000, 5000 -- Solution: Count by 1000: 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000. (e) four thousand fifty-six -- Solution: 4,056 = 4 thousand + 0 hundred + 5 tens + 6 ones = "four thousand fifty-six". [1 each]

Addition (4-digit). (a) 3845 -- Solution: 1456 + 2389. Ones: 6+9=15, carry 1. Tens: 5+8+1=14, carry 1. Hundreds: 4+3+1=8. Thousands: 1+2=3. Answer: 3845. (b) 5223 -- Solution: 3278 + 1945. Ones: 8+5=13, carry 1. Tens: 7+4+1=12, carry 1. Hundreds: 2+9+1=12, carry 1. Thousands: 3+1+1=5. Answer: 5223. (c) 7207 -- Solution: 4590 + 2617. Ones: 0+7=7. Tens: 9+1=10, carry 1. Hundreds: 5+6+1=12, carry 1. Thousands: 4+2+1=7. Answer: 7207. (d) 6000 -- Solution: 2009 + 3991. Ones: 9+1=10, carry 1. Tens: 0+9+1=10, carry 1. Hundreds: 0+9+1=10, carry 1. Thousands: 2+3+1=6. Answer: 6000. (e) 9103 -- Solution: 6378 + 2725. Ones: 8+5=13, carry 1. Tens: 7+2+1=10, carry 1. Hundreds: 3+7+1=11, carry 1. Thousands: 6+2+1=9. Answer: 9103. [1 each -- must show working]

Subtraction (4-digit). (a) 1522 -- Solution: 3000 - 1478. Ones: 0-8, borrow: 10-8=2. Tens: 9-7=2. Hundreds: 9-4=5. Thousands: 2-1=1. Answer: 1522. (b) 2335 -- Solution: 5200 - 2865. Ones: 0-5, borrow: 10-5=5. Tens: 9-6=3. Hundreds: 11-8=3. Thousands: 4-2=2. Answer: 2335. (c) 2001 -- Solution: 4000 - 1999. Ones: 0-9, borrow: 10-9=1. Tens: 9-9=0. Hundreds: 9-9=0. Thousands: 3-1=2. Answer: 2001. (d) 4222 -- Solution: 7500 - 3278. Ones: 0-8, borrow: 10-8=2. Tens: 9-7=2. Hundreds: 4-2=2 (after borrow from thousands, 5 becomes 4). Thousands: 7-3=4. Answer: 4222. (e) 4433 -- Solution: 9000 - 4567. Ones: 0-7, borrow: 10-7=3. Tens: 9-6=3. Hundreds: 9-5=4. Thousands: 8-4=4. Answer: 4433. [1 each -- must show working]

Multiplication (2-digit x 1-digit). (a) 270 -- Solution: 45 x 6. 5x6=30, write 0 carry 3. 4x6=24, +3=27. Answer: 270. (b) 312 -- Solution: 78 x 4. 8x4=32, write 2 carry 3. 7x4=28, +3=31. Answer: 312. (c) 736 -- Solution: 92 x 8. 2x8=16, write 6 carry 1. 9x8=72, +1=73. Answer: 736. (d) 603 -- Solution: 67 x 9. 7x9=63, write 3 carry 6. 6x9=54, +6=60. Answer: 603. (e) 588 -- Solution: 84 x 7. 4x7=28, write 8 carry 2. 8x7=56, +2=58. Answer: 588. [1 each]

Fractions. (a) 8 -- Solution: 1/2 of 16 = 16 / 2 = 8. (b) 7 -- Solution: 1/3 of 21 = 21 / 3 = 7. (c) 6 -- Solution: 1/4 of 24 = 24 / 4 = 6. (d) 6 stars -- Solution: 3/5 of 10 = (3 x 10) / 5 = 30 / 5 = 6 stars. (e) 2/3 -- Solution: Same denominator, bigger numerator = bigger fraction. 2/3 > 1/3. [1 each]

Money word problems. (a) Rs 100 -- Solution: Rs 25 x 4 = 25 + 25 + 25 + 25 = Rs 100. (b) Rs 155 -- Solution: Rs 500 - Rs 345. Ones: 0-5, borrow: 10-5=5. Tens: 9-4=5. Hundreds: 4-3=1. Answer: Rs 155. (c) Rs 165 -- Solution: Rs 120 + Rs 45 = 120 + 45. Ones: 0+5=5. Tens: 2+4=6. Hundreds: 1. Answer: Rs 165. (d) Rs 50 -- Solution: Rs 200 / 4 = 200/4 = Rs 50 per child. (e) Rs 25 -- Solution: Rs 200 - Rs 175. Ones: 0-5, borrow: 10-5=5. Tens: 9-7=2. Hundreds: 1-1=0. Answer: Rs 25. [1 each]

Time. (a) 60 minutes -- Solution: 1 hour = 60 minutes. (b) 60 seconds -- Solution: 1 minute = 60 seconds. (c) 5 hours -- Solution: From 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM = 8 to 12 = 4 hours + 1 hour = 5 hours. (d) 6:45 -- Solution: Short hand on 6 = hour 6. Long hand on 9 = 45 minutes. Time: 6:45. (e) 10:15 AM -- Solution: 9:30 + 45 minutes. 30 + 45 = 75 min = 1 hour 15 min. So 9:30 + 45 min = 10:00 + 15 min = 10:15 AM. [1 each]

Measurement. (a) 200 cm -- Solution: 2 m x 100 = 200 cm (1 m = 100 cm). (b) 3000 g -- Solution: 3 kg x 1000 = 3000 g (1 kg = 1000 g). (c) 75 cm -- Solution: 120 cm - 45 cm = 75 cm left. (d) 1250 ml -- Solution: 2 litres = 2000 ml. 2000 - 750 = 1250 ml left. (e) 1000 m -- Solution: 1 km = 1000 m. [1 each]

Word problems. (a) 772 books -- Solution: 1250 - 478. Ones: 0-8, borrow: 10-8=2. Tens: 4-7, borrow: 14-7=7. Hundreds: 11-4=7. Thousands: 0. Answer: 772. (b) 180 eggs -- Solution: 36 hens x 5 eggs = 36 x 5. 6x5=30, write 0 carry 3. 3x5=15, +3=18. Answer: 180. (c) 12 sweets -- Solution: 96 / 8. 8 x 12 = 96, so 96 / 8 = 12 sweets each. (d) 623 km -- Solution: 245 + 378. Ones: 5+8=13, carry 1. Tens: 4+7+1=12, carry 1. Hundreds: 2+3+1=6. Answer: 623. (e) 375 litres -- Solution: 500 - 125. Ones: 0-5, borrow: 10-5=5. Tens: 9-2=7. Hundreds: 4-1=3. Answer: 375. [1 each] VOCABULARY: place value, expanded form, addition, subtraction, multiplication, fractions, word problems, time, measurement, patterns. Fill in the blanks. (a) 5001, 5003 -- Solution: Count forward from 5000: 5000, 5001, 5002, 5003, 5004. Missing are 5001 and 5003. (b) 8000 -- Solution: In 8423, the digit 8 is in the thousands place. Place value = 8 x 1000 = 8000. (c) 10 -- Solution: 100 tens = 100 x 10 = 1000 = 10 hundred. (d) 500 -- Solution: 476 rounded to nearest hundred. Tens digit = 7 (>=5), so round up: 476 -> 500. (e) 9000 + 000 + 20 + 5 -- Solution: 9025 = 9 thousands + 0 hundreds + 2 tens + 5 ones = 9000 + 0 + 20 + 5. [1 each]

Addition (4-digit). (a) 5643 -- Solution: 3456 + 2187. Ones: 6+7=13, carry 1. Tens: 5+8+1=14, carry 1. Hundreds: 4+1+1=6. Thousands: 3+2=5. Answer: 5643. (b) 9134 -- Solution: 5678 + 3456. Ones: 8+6=14, carry 1. Tens: 7+5+1=13, carry 1. Hundreds: 6+4+1=11, carry 1. Thousands: 5+3+1=9. Answer: 9134. (c) 9124 -- Solution: 7890 + 1234. Ones: 0+4=4. Tens: 9+3=12, carry 1. Hundreds: 8+2+1=11, carry 1. Thousands: 7+1+1=9. Answer: 9124. (d) 10245 -- Solution: 4567 + 5678. Ones: 7+8=15, carry 1. Tens: 6+7+1=14, carry 1. Hundreds: 5+6+1=12, carry 1. Thousands: 4+5+1=10. Answer: 10245. (e) 10100 -- Solution: 9090 + 1010. Ones: 0+0=0. Tens: 9+1=10, carry 1. Hundreds: 0+0+1=1. Thousands: 9+1=10. Answer: 10100. [1 each]

Subtraction (4-digit). (a) 3556 -- Solution: 5432 - 1876. Ones: 2-6, borrow: 12-6=6. Tens: 2-7, borrow: 12-7=5. Hundreds: 3-8, borrow: 13-8=5. Thousands: 4-1=3. Answer: 3556. (b) 4544 -- Solution: 8000 - 3456. Ones: 0-6, borrow: 10-6=4. Tens: 9-5=4. Hundreds: 9-4=5. Thousands: 7-3=4. Answer: 4544. (c) 4522 -- Solution: 9200 - 4678. Ones: 0-8, borrow: 10-8=2. Tens: 9-7=2. Hundreds: 11-6=5. Thousands: 8-4=4. Answer: 4522. (d) 4241 -- Solution: 7000 - 2759. Ones: 0-9, borrow: 10-9=1. Tens: 9-5=4. Hundreds: 9-7=2. Thousands: 6-2=4. Answer: 4241. (e) 5817 -- Solution: 10000 - 4183. Ones: 0-3, borrow: 10-3=7. Tens: 9-8=1. Hundreds: 9-1=8. Thousands: 9-4=5. Answer: 5817. [1 each]

Fractions. (a) 4/5 -- Solution: 3/5 + 1/5. Same denominator, add numerators: 3+1=4. Answer: 4/5. (b) 4/8 = 1/2 -- Solution: 7/8 - 3/8. Same denominator: 7-3=4. Answer: 4/8 = 1/2 (simplify by dividing by 4). (c) 1/2 -- Solution: 2/4 = 2/2 / 4/2 = 1/2 (simplify by dividing numerator and denominator by 2). (d) 3/4 -- Solution: Compare 2/3 and 3/4. Common denominator 12: 2/3=8/12, 3/4=9/12. 9/12 > 8/12, so 3/4 is greater. (e) 4/8 -- Solution: 1/2 = ?/8. Multiply numerator and denominator by 4: 1x4/2x4 = 4/8. [1 each]

Word problems. (a) Rs7851 -- Solution: 4567 + 3284. Ones: 7+4=11, carry 1. Tens: 6+8+1=15, carry 1. Hundreds: 5+2+1=8. Thousands: 4+3=7. Answer: Rs7851. (b) 3822 toys -- Solution: 8500 - 4678. Ones: 0-8, borrow: 10-8=2. Tens: 9-7=2. Hundreds: 4-6, borrow: 14-6=8. Thousands: 7-4=3. Answer: 3822. (c) 840 chocolates -- Solution: 24 x 35. 24x5=120. 24x30=720. 120+720=840. (d) 24 pencils -- Solution: 168 / 7. 7 x 24 = 168, so 168 / 7 = 24. (e) 150 m -- Solution: Perimeter = 2 x (length + width) = 2 x (45 + 30) = 2 x 75 = 150 m. (f) 64 m^2 -- Solution: Area = side x side = 8 x 8 = 64 m^2. [2 each -- 1 method, 1 answer]

Convert units. (a) 300 cm -- Solution: 3 m x 100 = 300 cm (1 m = 100 cm). (b) 2000 g -- Solution: 2 kg x 1000 = 2000 g (1 kg = 1000 g). (c) 5000 ml -- Solution: 5 litres x 1000 = 5000 ml (1 L = 1000 ml). (d) 4 m -- Solution: 400 cm / 100 = 4 m (100 cm = 1 m). [1 each]

Time problems. (a) 6 hours -- Solution: 8:30 AM to 2:30 PM. 8:30 to 12:30 = 4 hours. 12:30 to 2:30 = 2 hours. Total = 6 hours. (b) 5:15 PM -- Solution: 3:00 PM + 2 hours 15 minutes = 5:00 PM + 15 min = 5:15 PM. [2 each] === ADDITIONAL PRACTICE QUESTIONS ===

Roman numerals. (a) XIV -- Solution: 14 = 10 + 4 = X + IV = XIV. (b) XXIX -- Solution: 29 = 10 + 10 + 9 = X + X + IX = XXIX. (c) 40 -- Solution: XL = 50 - 10 = 40 (X before L means subtract). (d) L -- Solution: 50 = L. (e) 99 -- Solution: XCIX = (100-10) + (10-1) = 90 + 9 = 99. [1 each]

Fill in the blanks. (a) 10,000 -- Solution: The smallest 5-digit number is 10000. (b) 60,000 -- Solution: In 76,543, digit 6 is in ten-thousands place. Value = 6 x 10000 = 60,000. (c) 100 -- Solution: 1 lakh = 100,000. 100,000 / 1000 = 100 thousand. (d) 9,000 -- Solution: 8765 rounded to nearest thousand. Hundreds digit = 7 (>=5), round up: 8765 -> 9000. (e) 40,000 + 5,000 + 600 + 70 + 8 -- Solution: 45678 = 4x10000 + 5x1000 + 6x100 + 7x10 + 8. [1 each]

Add and subtract (5-digit). (a) 19,134 -- Solution: 12345 + 6789. Ones: 5+9=14, carry 1. Tens: 4+8+1=13, carry 1. Hundreds: 3+7+1=11, carry 1. Thousands: 2+6+1=9. Ten-thousands: 1. Answer: 19134. (b) 40,245 -- Solution: 25678 + 14567. Ones: 8+7=15, carry 1. Tens: 7+6+1=14, carry 1. Hundreds: 6+5+1=12, carry 1. Thousands: 5+4+1=10, carry 1. Ten-thousands: 2+1+1=4. Answer: 40245. (c) 26,544 -- Solution: 50000 - 23456. Ones: 0-6, borrow: 10-6=4. Tens: 9-5=4. Hundreds: 9-4=5. Thousands: 9-3=6. Ten-thousands: 4-2=2. Answer: 26544. (d) 36,079 -- Solution: 75000 - 38921. Ones: 0-1, borrow: 10-1=9. Tens: 9-2=7. Hundreds: 9-9=0. Thousands: 14-8=6. Ten-thousands: 6-3=3. Answer: 36079. (e) 73,086 -- Solution: 43210 + 29876. Ones: 0+6=6. Tens: 1+7=8. Hundreds: 2+8=10, carry 1. Thousands: 3+9+1=13, carry 1. Ten-thousands: 4+2+1=7. Answer: 73086. [1 each]

HCF and LCM. (a) 8 -- Solution: Factors of 16: 1,2,4,8,16. Factors of 24: 1,2,3,4,6,8,12,24. HCF = 8 (largest common factor). (b) 24 -- Solution: Multiples of 6: 6,12,18,24,... Multiples of 8: 8,16,24,... LCM = 24 (smallest common multiple). (c) 9 -- Solution: Factors of 27: 1,3,9,27. Factors of 36: 1,2,3,4,6,9,12,18,36. HCF = 9. (d) 36 -- Solution: Multiples of 9: 9,18,27,36,... Multiples of 12: 12,24,36,... LCM = 36. (e) 7 -- Solution: Factors of 14: 1,2,7,14. Factors of 21: 1,3,7,21. HCF = 7. [1 each]

Fractions. (a) 7/6 = 1 1/6 -- Solution: 5/6 + 2/6. Same denominator: 5+2=7. Answer: 7/6 = 1 whole and 1/6. (b) 5/10 = 1/2 -- Solution: 9/10 - 4/10. Same denominator: 9-4=5. Answer: 5/10 = 1/2 (simplify by 5). (c) 3/4 -- Solution: 6/8 = 6/2 / 8/2 = 3/4 (simplify by dividing by 2). (d) 7/3 -- Solution: 2 1/3 = (2x3 + 1)/3 = 7/3 (improper fraction: whole x denominator + numerator). (e) 3/7 -- Solution: Same denominator, smaller numerator = smaller fraction. 3/7 < 4/7. [1 each]

Perimeter and area. (a) 46 cm -- Solution: Perimeter = 2 x (14 + 9) = 2 x 23 = 46 cm. (b) 48 cm -- Solution: Perimeter of square = 4 x side = 4 x 12 = 48 cm. (c) 300 cm^2 -- Solution: Area = length x width = 20 x 15 = 300 cm^2. (d) 225 m^2 -- Solution: Area = side x side = 15 x 15 = 225 m^2. (e) 12 cm -- Solution: Perimeter = 4 x side. Side = 48 / 4 = 12 cm. [1 each]

Money word problems. (a) Rs 1550 -- Solution: 5000 - 3450. Ones: 0-0=0. Tens: 0-5, borrow: 10-5=5. Hundreds: 9-4=5. Thousands: 4-3=1. Answer: Rs 1550. (b) Rs 25 -- Solution: 125 / 5 = Rs 25 per pen. (c) Rs 80 -- Solution: 640 / 8 = Rs 80 per box. (d) Rs 1450 -- Solution: 560 + 890. Ones: 0+0=0. Tens: 6+9=15, carry 1. Hundreds: 5+8+1=14, carry 1. Thousands: 0+0+1=1. Answer: Rs 1450. (e) Rs 725 -- Solution: 2000 - 1275. Ones: 0-5, borrow: 10-5=5. Tens: 9-7=2. Hundreds: 9-2=7. Thousands: 1-1=0. Answer: Rs 725. [1 each]

Time and measurement. (a) 200 minutes -- Solution: 3 hours x 60 + 20 = 180 + 20 = 200 minutes. (b) 2500 m -- Solution: 2 km x 1000 + 500 = 2000 + 500 = 2500 m. (c) 3 hours 30 minutes -- Solution: 9:45 AM to 1:15 PM. 9:45 to 12:45 = 3 hours. 12:45 to 1:15 = 30 min. Total = 3h 30m. (d) 5250 g -- Solution: 5 kg x 1000 + 250 = 5000 + 250 = 5250 g. (e) 2 hours 40 minutes -- Solution: 4:30 PM to 7:10 PM. 4:30 to 7:00 = 2h 30m. 7:00 to 7:10 = 10m. Total = 2h 40m. [1 each]

(b) 5472 toys -- Solution: 456 x 12. 456x2=912. 456x10=4560. 912+4560=5472. (c) 49 books -- Solution: 392 / 8. 8 x 49 = 392, so 392 / 8 = 49. (d) Perimeter = 200 m, Area = 2400 m^2 -- Solution: Perimeter = 2 x (60+40) = 2 x 100 = 200 m. Area = 60 x 40 = 2400 m^2. (e) 1625 litres -- Solution: 2500 - 875. Ones: 0-5, borrow: 10-5=5. Tens: 9-7=2. Hundreds: 14-8=6. Thousands: 1. Answer: 1625. Large numbers. (a) 100 -- Solution: 1 lakh = 100,000. 100,000 / 1000 = 100 thousand. (b) 10 -- Solution: 1 million = 10,00,000. 10,00,000 / 1,00,000 = 10 lakh. (c) 50,000 -- Solution: In 3,54,721, digit 5 is in ten-thousands place. Value = 5 x 10,000 = 50,000. (d) 4,57,000 -- Solution: 4,56,789 rounded to nearest thousand. Hundreds digit = 7 (>=5), round up: 4,56,789 -> 4,57,000. (e) Twenty-three lakh forty-five thousand six hundred seventy-eight -- Solution: 23,45,678 = 23 lakh + 45 thousand + 6 hundred + 78. [1 each]

HCF and LCM. (a) 6 -- Solution: Factors of 12: 1,2,3,4,6,12. Factors of 18: 1,2,3,6,9,18. HCF = 6. (b) 12 -- Solution: Factors of 24: 1,2,3,4,6,8,12,24. Factors of 36: 1,2,3,4,6,9,12,18,36. HCF = 12. (c) 12 -- Solution: Multiples of 4: 4,8,12,... Multiples of 6: 6,12,... LCM = 12. (d) 60 -- Solution: Multiples of 12: 12,24,36,48,60,... Multiples of 15: 15,30,45,60,... LCM = 60. (e) 5 -- Solution: Factors of 15: 1,3,5,15. Factors of 20: 1,2,4,5,10,20. HCF = 5. [1 each]

Fractions (all operations). (a) 13/12 -- Solution: 3/4 + 1/3. LCM of 4 and 3 = 12. 3/4 = 9/12, 1/3 = 4/12. 9/12 + 4/12 = 13/12. (b) 1/3 -- Solution: 5/6 - 1/2. LCM of 6 and 2 = 6. 1/2 = 3/6. 5/6 - 3/6 = 2/6 = 1/3 (simplify by 2). (c) 1/2 -- Solution: 2/3 x 3/4. Multiply numerators: 2x3=6. Multiply denominators: 3x4=12. 6/12 = 1/2 (simplify by 6). (d) 2 -- Solution: 4/5 / 2/5. Dividing fractions = multiply by reciprocal. 4/5 x 5/2 = 20/10 = 2. (e) 7/2 -- Solution: 3 1/2 = (3x2 + 1)/2 = 7/2 (improper fraction). [1 each]

Decimals. (a) 6.23 -- Solution: 3.45 + 2.78. Hundredths: 5+8=13, write 3 carry 1. Tenths: 4+7+1=12, write 2 carry 1. Ones: 3+2+1=6. Answer: 6.23. (b) 3.65 -- Solution: 7.50 - 3.85. Hundredths: 0-5, borrow: 10-5=5. Tenths: 4-8, borrow: 14-8=6. Ones: 6-3=3. Answer: 3.65. (c) 1.00 -- Solution: 0.25 x 4. 25 x 4 = 100. Two decimal places: 1.00. (d) 0.75 -- Solution: 3/4 = 3 / 4. 4 into 3.00: 4 goes into 30 seven times (28), remainder 2. 4 into 20 five times (20). Answer: 0.75. (e) 3/5 -- Solution: 0.6 = 6/10. Simplify by dividing by 2: 6/10 = 3/5. [1 each]

Final = 450 - 45 = Rs405. [marks as shown]

Large numbers. (a) forty-five lakh sixty-seven thousand eight hundred ninety -- Solution: 45,67,890 = 45 lakh + 67 thousand + 8 hundred + 90. (b) 34,05,612 -- Solution: Thirty-four lakh = 34,00,000. Five thousand = 5,000. Six hundred = 600. Twelve = 12. Total: 34,05,612. (c) 70,000 -- Solution: In 8,76,543, digit 7 is in ten-thousands place. Value = 7 x 10,000 = 70,000. (d) 5,67,900 -- Solution: 5,67,892 rounded to nearest hundred. Tens digit = 9 (>=5), round up: 5,67,892 -> 5,67,900. (e) 100 -- Solution: 1 crore = 100,00,000. 100,00,000 / 1,00,000 = 100 lakh. [1 each]

Decimals. (a) 21.35 -- Solution: 12.56 + 8.79. Hundredths: 6+9=15, carry 1. Tenths: 5+7+1=13, carry 1. Ones: 2+8+1=11, carry 1. Tens: 1+0+1=2. Answer: 21.35. (b) 10.65 -- Solution: 25.00 - 14.35. Hundredths: 0-5, borrow: 10-5=5. Tenths: 9-3=6. Ones: 4-4=0. Tens: 1-1=0. Answer: 10.65. (c) 21.0 -- Solution: 3.5 x 6. 35 x 6 = 210. One decimal place: 21.0. (d) 0.7 -- Solution: 7/10 = 0.7 (denominator 10 means one decimal place). (e) 9/20 -- Solution: 0.45 = 45/100. Simplify by 5: 45/100 = 9/20. [1 each]

Ratio and proportion. (a) 3:4 -- Solution: 45:60. Divide both by 15: 45/15=3, 60/15=4. Answer: 3:4. (b) Rs 420 -- Solution: 4 books = Rs 240. 1 book = 240/4 = Rs 60. 7 books = 60 x 7 = Rs 420. (c) Yes -- Solution: 10:15 = 2:3 (divide by 5). 20:30 = 2:3 (divide by 10). Both ratios equal, so in proportion. (d) A = Rs 720, B = Rs 480 -- Solution: Total parts = 3+2=5. 1 part = 1200/5 = Rs 240. A = 3x240 = Rs 720. B = 2x240 = Rs 480. (e) 40 -- Solution: 5 parts = 25. 1 part = 5. Larger = 8 x 5 = 40. [1 each]

Profit and loss. (a) Rs 150 -- Solution: Profit = SP - CP = 650 - 500 = Rs 150. (b) Rs 80 -- Solution: Loss = CP - SP = 800 - 720 = Rs 80. (c) Rs 1500 -- Solution: SP = CP + Profit = 1200 + 300 = Rs 1500. (d) Rs 200 -- Solution: SP = CP - Loss = 250 - 50 = Rs 200. (e) 20% -- Solution: Profit = 1800 - 1500 = Rs 300. Profit % = (300/1500) x 100 = 20%. [1 each]

Mensuration. (a) 48 cm^2 -- Solution: Area of triangle = 1/2 x base x height = 1/2 x 12 x 8 = 48 cm^2. (b) 900 cm^3 -- Solution: Volume = 15 x 10 x 6 = 900 cm^3. (c) 72 cm -- Solution: Perimeter of square = 4 x 18 = 72 cm. (d) 625 m^2 -- Solution: Area = 25 x 25 = 625 m^2. (e) 7500 m^2 -- Solution: Area = 100 x 75 = 7500 m^2. [1 each]

HCF and LCM. (a) 12 -- Solution: Factors of 36: 1,2,3,4,6,9,12,18,36. Factors of 48: 1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,48. HCF = 12. (b) 60 -- Solution: Multiples of 15: 15,30,45,60,... Multiples of 20: 20,40,60,... LCM = 60. (c) 14 -- Solution: Factors of 28: 1,2,4,7,14,28. Factors of 42: 1,2,3,6,7,14,21,42. HCF = 14. (d) 24 -- Solution: Multiples of 8: 8,16,24,... Multiples of 12: 12,24,... LCM = 24. (e) 16 -- Solution: Factors of 32: 1,2,4,8,16,32. Factors of 48: 1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,48. HCF = 16. [1 each]

Word problems. (a) 60 km/h -- Solution: Speed = distance / time = 240 / 4 = 60 km/h. (b) 10% -- Solution: 30 out of 300 = (30/300) x 100 = 3000/300 = 10%. (c) 60 m^3 -- Solution: Volume = 5 x 4 x 3 = 60 m^3. (d) 40% -- Solution: Saving = 15000 - 9000 = Rs 6000. % saved = (6000/15000) x 100 = 40%. (e) Rs 500 -- Solution: Loss = 20%, so SP = 80% of CP. CP = SP x (100/80) = 400 x 100/80 = 400 x 1.25 = Rs 500. [1 each]

Convert units. (a) 5600 m -- Solution: 5.6 km x 1000 = 5600 m. (b) 3250 g -- Solution: 3.25 kg x 1000 = 3250 g. (c) 2500 ml -- Solution: 2.5 litres x 1000 = 2500 ml. (d) 270 minutes -- Solution: 4 hours x 60 + 30 = 240 + 30 = 270 minutes. (e) 150 cm -- Solution: 1.5 m x 100 = 150 cm. Integers. (a) -4 -- Solution: (-7) + (+3). Different signs: subtract magnitudes: 7-3=4. Keep sign of larger: -4. (b) -13 -- Solution: (-5) + (-8). Same signs (both negative): add magnitudes: 5+8=13. Keep sign: -13. (c) 14 -- Solution: (+10) - (-4). Subtracting negative = adding positive: 10 + 4 = 14. (d) 18 -- Solution: (-6) x (-3). Negative x negative = positive. 6 x 3 = 18. (e) -3 -- Solution: (-24) / (+8). Negative / positive = negative. 24 / 8 = 3. Answer: -3. [1 each]

Fractions and Decimals. (a) 17/12 -- Solution: 2/3 + 3/4. LCM of 3 and 4 = 12. 2/3 = 8/12, 3/4 = 9/12. 8/12 + 9/12 = 17/12. (b) 1/2 -- Solution: 5/8 x 4/5. Multiply: 5x4=20, 8x5=40. 20/40 = 1/2 (simplify by 20). (c) 6.21 -- Solution: 3.75 + 2.46. Hundredths: 5+6=11, carry 1. Tenths: 7+4+1=12, carry 1. Ones: 3+2+1=6. Answer: 6.21. (d) 4.42 -- Solution: 8.00 - 3.58. Hundredths: 0-8, borrow: 10-8=2. Tenths: 9-5=4. Ones: 7-3=4. Answer: 4.42. (e) 0.35 -- Solution: 7/20 = 7 / 20. 20 into 7.00: 20 into 70 = 3 (60), remainder 10. 20 into 100 = 5. Answer: 0.35. [1 each]

Ratio and Proportion. (a) 2:3 -- Solution: 24:36. Divide both by 12: 24/12=2, 36/12=3. Answer: 2:3. (b) Rs 75 -- Solution: 3 pens = Rs 45. 1 pen = 45/3 = Rs 15. 5 pens = 15 x 5 = Rs 75. (c) Yes -- Solution: 15:20 = 3:4 (divide by 5). 30:40 = 3:4 (divide by 10). Both ratios equal, so in proportion. [marks as shown]

Algebra. (a) 22 -- Solution: x = 5. 3x + 7 = 3(5) + 7 = 15 + 7 = 22. (b) x = 7 -- Solution: x + 8 = 15. Subtract 8 from both sides: x = 15 - 8 = 7. (c) x = 8 -- Solution: 2x - 5 = 11. Add 5: 2x = 16. Divide by 2: x = 8. (d) 3y + 5 -- Solution: "5 more than 3 times y" = 3y + 5. (e) y = 7 -- Solution: 3y = 21. Divide both sides by 3: y = 21/3 = 7. [1 each]

Geometry. (a) 180 deg  -- Solution: The sum of angles in any triangle is always 180 deg . (b) equilateral -- Solution: A triangle with all three sides equal is called an equilateral triangle. (c) 180 deg  -- Solution: Angles on a straight line add up to 180 deg . (d) parallelogram -- Solution: A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel is a parallelogram. (e) right-angled scalene -- Solution: One angle is 90 deg  (right-angled) and all sides are different (scalene). [1 each]

Mensuration. (a) 40 cm -- Solution: Perimeter = 2 x (length + width) = 2 x (12 + 8) = 2 x 20 = 40 cm. (b) 90 cm^2 -- Solution: Area = length x width = 15 x 6 = 90 cm^2. (c) 81 cm^2 -- Solution: Area = side x side = 9 x 9 = 81 cm^2. (d) 200 cm^3 -- Solution: Volume = 10 x 5 x 4 = 200 cm^3. (e) 44 cm -- Solution: Circumference = 2pir = 2 x (22/7) x 7 = 2 x 22 = 44 cm. [1 each]

Word problems. (a) Rs13500 earned, Rs5500 saved -- Solution: Earnings = 450 x 30 = Rs13500. Saving = 13500 - 8000 = Rs5500. (b) 600 litres used, 900 left -- Solution: Used = 2/5 x 1500 = 600 litres. Left = 1500 - 600 = 900 litres. (c) 12 girls, 30 total -- Solution: Ratio 3:2. 3 parts = 18 boys, so 1 part = 6. Girls = 2 x 6 = 12. Total = 18 + 12 = 30. (d) Rs1290 -- Solution: Perimeter = 2 x (25+18) = 2 x 43 = 86 m. Cost = 86 x 15 = Rs1290. (e) x = 4 -- Solution: 4x + 3 = 19. Subtract 3: 4x = 16. Divide by 4: x = 4. [3 each -- 1-2 method, 1 answer]

Data Handling. (a) Mean = 60 -- Solution: Mean = (45+60+75+50+70)/5 = 300/5 = 60. (b) Median = 60 -- Solution: Sort: 45, 50, 60, 70, 75. Middle value (3rd) = 60. (c) Range = 30 -- Solution: Range = highest - lowest = 75 - 45 = 30. (d) No mode -- Solution: All values appear exactly once, so there is no mode. [marks as shown]

Geometry construction. (a) Equilateral triangle -- Solution: Draw AB = 7 cm. With compass, draw arc from A with radius 7 cm. Draw arc from B with radius 7 cm. Intersection = C. Join AC and BC. All sides = 7 cm. [3] (b) 60 deg  angle -- Solution: Draw a base line. Place protractor centre at vertex. Mark 60 deg  on the scale. Draw ray from vertex through the mark. Label the angle. Integers. (a) -4 -- Solution: (-12) + (+8). Different signs: subtract: 12-8=4. Keep sign of larger (-12): -4. (b) 20 -- Solution: (+15) - (-5). Subtracting negative = adding positive: 15 + 5 = 20. (c) 28 -- Solution: (-7) x (-4). Negative x negative = positive. 7 x 4 = 28. (d) 6 -- Solution: (-36) / (-6). Negative / negative = positive. 36 / 6 = 6. (e) -5, -2, 0, 3, 7 -- Solution: Ascending order (smallest to largest). Negative numbers come before zero, which comes before positives. [1 each]

Algebra. (a) 44 -- Solution: x = 4. 2x^2 + 3x = 2(16) + 3(4) = 32 + 12 = 44. (b) x = 7 -- Solution: 3x - 7 = 14. Add 7: 3x = 21. Divide by 3: x = 7. (c) x = 27 -- Solution: x/3 = 9. Multiply both sides by 3: x = 9 x 3 = 27. (d) 5x + 7 -- Solution: 5(x + 2) - 3 = 5x + 10 - 3 = 5x + 7 (distribute 5, then simplify). (e) x = 5 -- Solution: 2(x + 3) = 16. Distribute: 2x + 6 = 16. Subtract 6: 2x = 10. Divide by 2: x = 5. [1 each]

Ratio and proportion. (a) 2:3 -- Solution: 48:72. Divide both by 24: 48/24=2, 72/24=3. Answer: 2:3. (b) Rs 4800 -- Solution: 6 workers = Rs 3600. 1 worker = 3600/6 = Rs 600. 8 workers = 600 x 8 = Rs 4800. (c) Yes -- Solution: 12:18 = 2:3 (divide by 6). 16:24 = 2:3 (divide by 8). Both equal, so in proportion. (d) Rs 500, Rs 750, Rs 250 -- Solution: Total parts = 2+3+1=6. 1 part = 1500/6 = Rs 250. Shares: 2x250=500, 3x250=750, 1x250=250. (e) 15 cm and 10 cm -- Solution: Sides = 3x and 2x. Perimeter = 2(3x + 2x) = 10x = 50. x = 5. Sides = 15 cm and 10 cm. [1 each]

Geometry. (a) 55 deg  -- Solution: Complement = 90 deg  - 35 deg  = 55 deg  (complementary angles sum to 90 deg ). (b) 70 deg  -- Solution: Supplement = 180 deg  - 110 deg  = 70 deg  (supplementary angles sum to 180 deg ). (c) Scalene -- Solution: All three sides are different (5, 6, 7), so it is a scalene triangle. (d) 360 deg  -- Solution: The sum of angles in any quadrilateral is 360 deg . (e) Isosceles -- Solution: A triangle with two equal sides and one different is an isosceles triangle. [1 each]

Mensuration. (a) 63 cm^2 -- Solution: Area of triangle = 1/2 x base x height = 1/2 x 14 x 9 = 63 cm^2. (b) 44 cm -- Solution: Circumference = pi x diameter = (22/7) x 14 = 22 x 2 = 44 cm. (c) 480 cm^3 -- Solution: Volume = 12 x 8 x 5 = 480 cm^3. (d) 225 cm^2 -- Solution: Area = 15 x 15 = 225 cm^2. (e) 39 cm -- Solution: Perimeter = 3 x 13 = 39 cm (equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides). [1 each]

Data handling. (a) Mean = 66.67 -- Solution: Mean = (55+70+65+80+55+75)/6 = 400/6 = 66.67. (b) Median = 67.5 -- Solution: Sort: 55, 55, 65, 70, 75, 80. Even count, so median = average of middle two = (65+70)/2 = 67.5. (c) Mode = 55 -- Solution: 55 appears twice (most frequent), so mode = 55. (d) Range = 25 -- Solution: Range = 80 - 55 = 25. (e) 80 -- Solution: The highest score is 80. [1 each]

Word problems. (a) Revenue = Rs 5400, Profit = Rs 1350 -- Solution: Revenue = 45 x 120 = Rs 5400. Total CP = 45 x 90 = Rs 4050. Profit = 5400 - 4050 = Rs 1350. (b) 60 km/h, 16.67 m/s -- Solution: Speed = 180/3 = 60 km/h. Convert: 60 x (5/18) = 300/18 = 16.67 m/s. (c) Width = 9 cm, Perimeter = 50 cm -- Solution: Width = 144/16 = 9 cm. Perimeter = 2 x (16+9) = 2 x 25 = 50 cm. (d) x = 5 -- Solution: 3(2x - 5) = 15. Distribute: 6x - 15 = 15. Add 15: 6x = 30. Divide by 6: x = 5. (e) Used = 450 litres, Left = 750 litres -- Solution: Used = 3/8 x 1200 = 450 litres. Left = 1200 - 450 = 750 litres. [1 each]

Simplify. (a) 3/5 -- Solution: 6/5 - 3/10 = 12/10 - 3/10 = 9/10. Then 2/3 x 9/10 = 18/30 = 3/5 (simplify by 6). (b) 35 -- Solution: Use distributive property: 3.5 x (2.4 + 7.6) = 3.5 x 10 = 35. (c) 25 -- Solution: (-5) x [(-3) + (-2)] = (-5) x (-5) = 25 (negative x negative = positive). (d) 3 -- Solution: 0.75 / 0.25 = 75/100 / 25/100 = 75/25 = 3. (e) 25/36 -- Solution: LCM of 12, 18, 6 = 36. 7/12 = 21/36, 5/18 = 10/36, 1/6 = 6/36. 21/36 + 10/36 - 6/36 = 25/36. question_text: Triangles -- Angle Properties. [4] (a) The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2:3:4. Find each angle. [2] (b) In triangle PQR, angleP = 50 deg , angleQ = 60 deg . Find the exterior angle at R. [2]
answer_text: Solution: angleR = 180 deg  - 50 deg  - 60 deg  = 70 deg . Exterior angle at R = 180 deg  - 70 deg  = 110 deg . (Alternatively, exterior angle = sum of two remote interior angles = 50 deg  + 60 deg  = 110 deg .)

question_text: Congruence of Triangles. [4] (a) In triangles ABC and DEF, AB = DE, BC = EF, and angleB = angleE. State the congruence criterion and write the congruence relation. [2] (b) In triangles PQR and STU, PQ = ST, QR = TU, and PR = SU. State the congruence criterion. [2]
answer_text: Solution: All three sides of one triangle are equal to the corresponding three sides of the other. By SSS (Side-Side-Side) criterion, trianglePQR ~= triangleSTU.

question_text: Data Handling -- Mean, Median, Mode. [4] The marks of 8 students are: 42, 55, 42, 68, 75, 55, 42, 90. (a) Find the mean. [1] (b) Find the median. [1] (c) Find the mode. [1] (d) Find the range. [1]
answer_text: Solution: Range = maximum - minimum = 90 - 42 = 48.

question_text: Probability. [4] (a) A bag contains 5 red, 3 blue, and 2 green marbles. One marble is drawn at random. Find the probability of drawing: (i) a red marble, (ii) a blue marble, (iii) a green marble. [3] (b) A coin is tossed. What is the probability of getting a tail? [1]
answer_text: Solution: A coin has 2 outcomes (Head, Tail). P(Tail) = 1/2.

answer_text: Solution: Side = cbrt729 = 9 cm. TSA = 6 x side^2 = 6 x 81 = 486 cm^2.

question_text: Mensuration -- Cylinders. [4] (a) Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 5 cm and height 14 cm. (pi = 22/7) [2] (b) Find the total surface area of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (pi = 22/7) [2]
